sam: heads-up, i'm running an experiment for adaptive workspace sizing on the serving runtime to cut peak GPU mem for long-context workloads. short notes and a config snippet below.

sam: config (WIP):
```json
{
  \"adaptive_workspace\": true,
  \"min_workspace_mb\": 64,
  \"max_workspace_mb\": 2048,
  \"growth_policy\": \"per-request-percentile\", // grow to 90th pct of recent needs
  \"shrink_threshold\": 0.55, // don't shrink below this utilization
  \"oom_soft_limit_pct\": 0.95 // trigger conservative mode before hard OOMs
}
```

sam: quick observations: peak mem down ~18% on b4-longseq canary, but p95 latency bumped a bit and some CPU copying increased.

jia: nice. what's the fallback if adaptive growth fails during an allocation? :eyes:

sam: fallback is the legacy fixed workspace for that device; also added a soft OOM counter per-tenant that flips conservative mode (no shrinking, pre-reserve kv slab).

mike: can you paste the perf numbers (p50/p95/tokens-s)?

sam: before (fixed ws): p50 28ms p95 110ms tokens/s 1200;
after (adaptive): p50 30ms p95 125ms tokens/s 1150;
peak mem: -18% avg across canary nodes. tail-latency regression concentrated on sequences with lots of kv refills.

anya: hmm, KV cache behavior might be the culprit — if workspace shrinks mid-seq we might force extra KV refills which inflates token latency. did you simulate long cache-hit patterns?

sam: good call. in the current run we pin kv cache into a reserved slab when tenant is in conservative mode. also added a check to avoid shrink if kv_active_bytes > 0.6 * kv_reserved_bytes.

mike: any interactions with kernel selection? i've seen kernels pick a slower matmul path when workspace is small which kills perf for certain hidden sizes.

sam: yeah — added a kernel-selector hint: effective_workspace_size gets factored into kernel scoring. results: avoids pathological kernel switches but costs ~2% on very small batches. overall helps stability.

perf-bot: perf-bot: canary run #42 finished. regression flagged: model=b4-longseq, p95 +12% under 8 concurrent clients. trace: canary/2098765432/42

anya: @sam can you try a warm-up policy that grows workspace proactively during tail-heavy sequences? also try our batching heuristic "tail-preserve" which keeps KV-locality for long seqs.

sam: will do. planned: re-run canary on mon with tail-preserve, kernel-hint, and kv pinning. command i'll use: `run_canary --config adaptive_workspace.json --clients 8 --seq_len 4096 --batching tail-preserve`

sam: thanks all — i'll post the canary results and a short PR with configs. :thumbsup:
